-87.97830,41.84540.name: Reproductive Medicine Institute
-87.97830,41.84540.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Elena Trukhacheva, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

77.24207,28.56531.name: Birla Fertility & IVF
77.24207,28.56531.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-75.38881,40.08512.name: Franklin Biolabs Inc.
-75.38881,40.08512.state: KING OF PRUSSIA, PA, UNITED STATES
-75.38881,40.08512.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-71.88674,45.41038.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, February 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-77.04000,38.90000.name: United States — USDA APHIS — licensed research facilities
-77.04000,38.90000.desc: Every registered US research facility is named, inspected, and reports annually how many dogs, cats, primates and other covered animals it used and in what pain category. The inspection reports are published per facility, specific, and almost never read. Mice, rats and birds bred for research are excluded from the governing Act, so the most detailed facility register in the world omits the overwhelming majority of the animals used in it.

-77.04000,38.90000.name: Engineered petunias — second wave found after the first recall
-77.04000,38.90000.type: Ornamental plant, unapproved variety in trade
-77.04000,38.90000.size: Further varieties on sale years after the first clearance
-77.04000,38.90000.desc: A second wave of engineered petunias found in the United States and Europe after the first recall, showing the material had never been fully removed from the ornamental trade.

-122.27000,37.80600.name: Pivot Bio
-122.27000,37.80600.desc: Sells engineered soil bacteria that fix nitrogen, applied to seed across millions of US acres. By area it is among the largest deliberate releases of an engineered organism in history — and it generates no entry in any biosafety register anywhere, because a microbe on a seed is not a plant and coating it is not planting. The scale and the invisibility are facts about the same product.

-122.27000,37.80600.name: Eat Just / GOOD Meat
-122.27000,37.80600.desc: The first company to sell cultivated meat anywhere, in Singapore in 2020, and later cleared in the United States. Singapore approved it because a city-state importing most of its food has reasons a farming country does not — which is why the first approval was never going to come from a large agricultural producer.

-70.71600,42.61800.name: New England Biolabs
-70.71600,42.61800.desc: An employee-owned company supplying the enzymes molecular biology is done with, including many of the restriction enzymes and polymerases that made the field possible. Its ownership structure is the unusual part: a central supplier to a heavily consolidated industry that has stayed independent and prices its catalogue accordingly.

4.95500,52.35500.name: uniQure
4.95500,52.35500.desc: Produced Glybera, approved in Europe in 2012 as the first gene therapy licensed anywhere in the Western world. It was withdrawn in 2017 having been used by a handful of patients — priced at around a million dollars, for a condition too rare to sustain it. The first approval and the first commercial failure are the same product.
